The agency announced a record number of awards to early-career investigators this year, committing more than $400 million to support 1,200 scientists at the start of their independent research careers. The awards are intended to help new investigators launch laboratories and pursue ambitious projects at a stage when funding is often hardest to secure. Officials also unveiled a new recruitment initiative to bring promising young researchers into the agency’s own laboratories, offering protected time and dedicated resources for the first five years. “Investing in the next generation of scientists is essential to the future of biomedical research,” said the director. Applications for the recruitment program open next month, and selection will be based on scientific promise, mentorship plans, and fit with institutional priorities.
